newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania's king says president agrees to referendum.
newsitem.headline: Albania's king says president agrees to referendum.

text.p: Albania's King Leka said on Friday that President Sali Berisha has agreed to hold a referendum asking Albanians whether they want to restore the monarchy 58 years after Leka's father fled the country.

King Leka said after a 50-minute meeting with Berisha on Friday that the president was willing to allow Albanians to vote on the issue. But he said the political parties and Berisha would still have to determine the timing of the referendum.

"The meeting was warm and friendly," Leka said in an interview with Reuters. "He said the referendum would be on the agenda and would be carried out. But it would be up to the political partners and himself as to when that would happen."

King Leka returned from exile last week and has called for the monarchy to be restored as a way to unify the country, shattered by months of violence following the collapse of dubious investment schemes.

"I would prefer that the referendum takes place before the elections," King Leka said, referring to early general elections scheduled to take place in June. "But I understand the limitations on the authorities, therefore whichever works out."
King Leka was only days old when his father, King Zog, fled with his family in 1939.
